title: Client & server
hook: Every app on your phone is really just a conversation between two computers.

steps.caption: You tap something. Your phone sends a request out onto the network.

nodeCaptions.client: The client: whatever asked for something — a phone, a laptop, a smartwatch.
nodeCaptions.server: A server is just a computer that's always on, waiting to answer requests.

steps.caption: The server does its work, then sends something back.

nodeCaptions.server: It figured out what you asked for and packaged up an answer.
nodeCaptions.client: Your phone receives the response and shows it to you.

takeaways: "Client" just means whoever is asking. "Server" just means whoever is listening and answering.
Almost everything else in networking is a variation on this one request-response shape.
A server can be answering thousands of clients at once — it doesn't know or care which app you're using.

quiz.question: What makes a computer a "server"?
choices: It's more powerful hardware than a client
It's a computer that listens for requests and responds to them
It's only used by companies, never by individuals
It doesn't have an operating system
quiz.explanation: Server is a role, not a hardware spec — any computer that listens for and answers requests is acting as a server.
